Most of my clients live in a different time zone than I do.
Jakarta, Berlin, New York, Sydney. For a long time my “system” was a world clock, a to-do app, a spreadsheet for hours and a separate tool for invoices. I kept asking myself the same question every day: what time is it for my client right now, and when should I send this?
So I built the tool I wanted. Meet Taskly  😊 
Under the hood: React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind and Supabase, deployed on Cloudflare. It works offline first, syncs in real time across devices, and every table is protected with Row Level Security.
What I learned: the hardest part of remote freelancing isn’t the work itself. It’s the coordination around it. Good tools should quietly remove that friction.

As we gather in Antalya on 17 November 2026  for #COP31, LiRWOCA and Value Network Ventures (VNV) hosted a side event at the Liberia Pavilion: From Framework to Finance: Unlocking Private Capital for Blue Carbon in Liberia.

The session looked at how Liberia can turn its carbon market frameworks into private finance for mangroves and coastal ecosystems, with coastal communities benefiting from the start.
Mangroves, lagoons and wetlands sustain coastal livelihoods and protect communities like West Point in Monrovia from storms and erosion. Yet their carbon value remains largely untapped. Liberia has set up a Carbon Markets Authority, a national carbon market policy and NDC 3.0. The next step is finance that flows.

We opened with lessons from Indonesia and heard from:
🎙️ Emmanuel D.Wilson (Moderator)

🔹 Dr. Meilinda Suriani Harefa, Founder and Executive Director, YAKOPI

🔹 Madam Jeanine M. Cooper, CEO, Carbon Markets Authority

🔹 Norwu Kolu Harris, NDC Partnership In-Country Facilitator, Environmental Protection Agency

🔹 Shreya Dutta, Head of Programs, Value Network Ventures

🔹 Yundeh Butler, Executive Director, LiRWOCA

Madam Jeanine M. Cooper, Presidential Envoy on Climate Action and CEO of the Carbon Markets Authority, shared how Liberia's carbon market approach will work for investors and developers, and how benefits will reach coastal communities.

Key messages from the session:

✅ Liberia's frameworks are in place; the focus now is turning them into investable blue carbon projects

✅ Early-stage risk must be shared to attract the first private investment

✅ Coastal communities must be partners from day one, with their restoration and monitoring work recognised and paid for.

Thank you to everyone who joined us, our speakers, and the Liberia Pavilion team.

At COP31 in Antalya, 75 countries had, as of 18 Nov, backed a voluntary "35 by 35" goal for electricity to reach 35% of global final energy consumption by 2035. Argus noted that the pledge does not directly reference clean energy.

An IEA report published on 9 Nov says electricity's share of Southeast Asia's final energy use rose from 12% in 2000 to 25% in 2025, above the 23% global average. On today's policies and technology trends, it is set to reach 32% by 2035, short of the global 35% goal; in the IEA's High Electrification Scenario it reaches 41%. Coal-fired power met over 60% of the region's electricity demand growth over the past decade and now accounts for almost half of generation. Renewables met around 40% of new demand and now supply over a quarter of generation.

The Philippines joined on 18 Nov, provided the pledge remains voluntary and each country sets its own path. In Indonesia, President Director of PT PLN (Persero) Suroso Isnandar asked Institut Teknologi PLN (ITPLN) to study the pledge so it can be carried out — a utility request, not a government endorsement.

For Singapore and Malaysia buyers, including data centres and industrial users, faster electrification means more power to contract, but higher electricity use is not the same as cleaner power. For Malaysian renewable energy developers and suppliers serving Singapore offtake, a rising electricity share can support demand for new capacity, but extra demand can still be met by coal, as much of the last decade's growth was. Offtake contracts and cross-border electricity imports can support a seller's offtake, but a buyer's renewable claim rests on I-REC certificates cancelled in its name, not on the contract or the import alone.

Why is the focus on Asean more and more as China's property woes, SI's spy, deflating local consumption, $1 trillion trade surplus with the rest of the world, etc. building a global disinterest in the 2nd biggest economy. Asean is a 11 country bloc with new interest, focus, as countries comprise of commodity developer, manufacturing builder, tourists' favourite, rich financial centre, etc., etc.

Metals and Energy
• Nickel and Ferroalloys: Leading global supply and battery-grade refining for electric vehicles.
• Coal: Major energy export, especially to Asian markets.
• Mineral Fuels and Oils: Includes liquefied natural gas (LNG), crude oil, and refined petroleum.
• Precious and Base Metals: Gold, silver, copper, bauxite, aluminum, tin, and iron/steel products.
Agriculture and Forestry
• Palm Oil: The world's top producer and exporter, used in food, biofuels, and manufacturing.
• Rubber: Natural rubber for tires and industrial goods.
• Coffee and Cocoa: Major exports, including specialty coffee origins and processed cocoa products.
• Spices and Crops: Cloves, cinnamon, nutmeg, tea, tobacco, cassava, and rice (key to domestic food security).
• Forestry and Fisheries: Teak and wood products, furniture, bioenergy pellets, and seafood such as shrimp.

2) Vietnam is touted as the next manufacturing hub as factories increasingly moved from China to set up their base. It is also the 2nd biggest rice exporter of the world. Vietnam's GDP growth has reached above 8%!
3) Thailand is a tourists' favourite. It consistently ranks as the number 1 tourist hot-spot in the world. Thailand is also world's 3rd largest rice exporter.
4) Singapore is the 4th financial centre in the world, after London, New York and Hong Kong. Previously, it rose to 3rd. Singapore concentrates on tech value manufacturing and GDP growth stays consistently above 5% for the past couple of years. Also touted as one of the richest countries per capital income in the world, as home ownership stays above 92%. Singapore is also a top petroleum refinery and oil trading hub.
5) Cambodia is 5th largest rice exporter in the world. Cambodia and Laos have a trade treaty with Thailand and rice exports and hydropower energy remain vital pillars of their economies. Cambodia has a GDP growth above 5% and Laos above 4%.
6) Malaysia is the latest favourite for chip factories and data centres. Malaysia's GDP growth maintains above 5%.

Unity is something the region sought tooth and nail to maintain, with differing economic goals. The bloc believes that as the world becomes more fragmented, the bloc must insists on cooperating more. Staying united, the group looks ahead to more breakthroughs in the region's payment system, energy sharing, food security, SI adoption in key industries, and greater prosperity together.

Can you still sideload apps on Android? Yes, and the rule that worries people is narrower than it sounds.

Since 30 September 2026, Google's developer verification has been enforced in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand. It links every app on a certified Android device to a real person or company: a government ID for individuals, a D-U-N-S number for organisations, a one-time $25 fee, and a free limited account for students and hobbyists that can share apps with up to 20 devices. Google checks who made the app, not what it does.

The first phase covers only seven participating stores. An APK downloaded from a website is not checked yet, and installs over a USB cable with ADB are untouched. The global rollout to all apps on certified devices is promised for 2027, with no countries or dates named.

For unverified apps there is a one-time advanced flow: developer mode on, confirm nobody is coaching you, restart, wait one day, confirm with a fingerprint or PIN, then allow installs for seven days or indefinitely. Each step is built to interrupt a scam call rather than to stop you.

Scientific and Quranic Reflections on Energy in Nature, Ourselves and Clean Energy We Need

From the leaves in our forests to the blood in our veins—and now to the future of zero-carbon hydrogen—one element quietly powers life and industry: Iron (Fe). 🌍🩸⚡

When we look closely at how nature engineers energy, a remarkable unity emerges:

🌱1. Energy in Nature (Plants): Iron is an essential micronutrient that drives chlorophyll synthesis, allowing plants to capture sunlight and convert it into life-sustaining energy.

🩸2. Energy Within Ourselves (Humans): In our bloodstream, iron sits at the core of hemoglobin, binding oxygen in our lungs and delivering it to every cell to fuel ATP production.

🔬3. Shared Molecular Harmony: At the molecular level, the chlorin ring in chlorophyll and the heme group in human blood share a nearly identical porphyrin structure—a striking reminder of the reflection inQuran (51:20–21): "There are countless signs on earth for those with sure faith, as there are within yourselves. Can you not see?"

⚡ 4. Inspiring the Future of Clean Energy:

Beyond sustaining biology, Quran (Al-Hadid 57:25) highlights iron as possessing "Ba'sun Shadid"—mighty power and immense benefits for humankind. Today, modern sustainable engineering is unlocking this exact potential through theSteam-Iron Loop:

Clean Hydrogen Generation: Passing steam (H2O) over metallic iron (Fe) oxidizes it into magnetite (Fe3O4), releasing pure, carbon-free hydrogen (H2).

Circular Energy Storage: Using renewable energy, magnetite can be reduced back into metallic iron—creating a safe, recyclable, high-density energy carrier without the storage hurdles of compressed gas.

At BioCom Indonesia, we believe the best engineering solutions mirror nature’s closed-loop efficiency—turning timeless wisdom and fundamental chemistry into practical, zero-waste infrastructure for a cleaner tomorrow.
